weeks.title: Environmental Concerns, Population Growth and Resource Consumption
examFlags: Pn = P0 + nX (arithmetic/linear)
Pn = P0(1+r)^n geometric vs Pn = P0 e^(rn) exponential
IPAT: I = P x A x T (Ehrlich and Holdren, 1971)
Ecological footprint in global hectares (gha); biocapacity vs demand
Earth Overshoot Day: demand exceeds year's biocapacity
Global ~2.8 gha footprint/person vs ~1.6 gha biocapacity/person
EPI = annual energy use / floor area (kWh/m^2-y)
MC Mehta vs UOI 1991 -> env education mandate
R^2 > 0.9 good fit; > 0.95 very good for population curve-fitting

concepts.name: Sustainable development (course framing)
concepts.note: Course objective: incorporate sustainable development into daily decisions and remain sensitive to pollution impacts. Capital-stock idea: live off interest of environment+economy+society capital, not the capital itself. Principles include maximize renewables, minimize non-renewables, maintain biodiversity, population control, and nutrient cycling.

concepts.name: Population growth models
concepts.note: Arithmetic/linear: fixed increment X each period for planned/controlled growth. Geometric: discrete constant percent growth Pn=P0(1+r)^n. Exponential: continuous Pn=P0 e^(rn); for same r, exponential > geometric. India census 1911-2011 often fit exponential (R^2>0.95) with ~1.75%/y total and ~2.85%/y urban.

concepts.name: IPAT model
concepts.note: Environmental Impact = Population x Affluence x Technology. Affluence proxies: per-capita energy or MSW; Technology proxies: carbon per kWh or energy/GDP. Example: CO2/y = Pop x fossil electricity per capita x kg CO2/kWh. Disaggregated growth rates multiply (India example ~5%/y CO2 growth).

concepts.name: Ecological footprint and Overshoot Day
concepts.note: EF tracks biologically productive land/water needed to produce resources and absorb wastes (incl. carbon), in global hectares. EFproduction = P x EQF / Yw. Earth Overshoot Day is when cumulative demand exceeds what Earth regenerates that year; dates shifted earlier over decades (late July recent years; 22 Aug 2020 COVID anomaly).

concepts.name: EPI and LCA
concepts.note: Energy Performance Index normalizes building/campus electricity to floor area (kWh/m^2-y) using multi-year bills. Lifecycle Assessment inventories inputs/outputs from raw materials through use to disposal.

definitions.definition: A contaminant is present where it does not belong or above natural background; a pollutant causes adverse effects or unreasonable interference at given concentration/duration.
Urban areas significantly warmer than surrounding rural areas due to built surfaces, waste heat and altered energy balance.
Capacity of ecosystems to regenerate useful biological materials and absorb wastes, in global hectares.
Productivity-adjusted hectare with world-average productivity, used to compare different land types.
Natural capital is the stock of environmental assets; natural services are ecosystem functions supporting human well-being.

comparisons.title: Arithmetic vs Geometric vs Exponential growth

numbers.label: India avg annual pop growth (census fit)
Global EF vs biocapacity per person

mustRemember: IPAT: I=P x A x T -- know what A and T can represent
Geometric != exponential: e^(rn) grows faster than (1+r)^n for same r
EF units = global hectares; include carbon land
Of 30 most polluted cities, ~21 in India (course claim)

weeks.title: Principles of Sustainable Development
examFlags: Brundtland 1987: meets present needs without compromising future generations
Rio Earth Summit 1992 adopted sustainable development agenda
MDGs 2000 -> SDGs 2015 (17 goals, 2030 Agenda)
Nine planetary boundaries; safe operating space (Rockstrom/Steffen)
Anthropocene Great Acceleration in socio-economic and Earth-system indicators
Three pillars: environment, economy, society
Six SDG transformations bridge multiple goals

concepts.name: Brundtland definition and evolution
concepts.note: UN Brundtland Commission (1983) report Our Common Future (1987) coined the classic SD definition. Institutionalized at Rio 1992, advanced via MDGs (2000), then universal SDGs adopted by all UN Member States in 2015 with targets to 2030.

concepts.name: Planetary boundaries
concepts.note: Define a safe operating space for humanity with respect to Earth-system processes. Crossing boundaries increases risk of abrupt/irreversible change. Inner green zone = proposed safe space across nine biophysical processes.

concepts.name: Anthropocene / Great Acceleration
concepts.note: Trends ~1750-2010 show steep rises in population, GDP, energy, fertilizer use alongside Earth-system changes (CO2, N2O, methane, temperature, deforestation). Frames why boundaries and SDGs became necessary.

concepts.name: SDGs structure
concepts.note: 17 goals from No Poverty (#1) through Partnerships (#17). Implementation uses indicator frameworks (2017) and six transformations mapping onto multiple SDGs -- dropping any transformation hurts several goals.

definitions.definition: Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs (Brundtland, 1987).
Quantified limits on Earth-system processes that define a safe operating space for humanity.
Composite progress measure aggregating country performance across SDG indicators.
Interdependent environmental, economic and social dimensions that must be balanced.

comparisons.title: MDGs vs SDGs
rows: Adds climate, oceans, cities, justice, partnerships

mustRemember: Nine planetary boundaries concept (names > exact numbers)
SDG #6 water, #7 energy, #11 cities, #12 SCP, #13 climate -- frequent env links
Sustainability requires all three pillars, not environment alone

weeks.title: Understanding Air Pollution
examFlags: Ambient air = outdoor atmospheric air supporting life
Primary vs secondary pollutants (e.g., O3, secondary PM)
Criteria air pollutants vs hazardous/non-criteria
Sources: stationary, mobile, area
ESP / baghouse / scrubbers / FGD control options
Montreal Protocol 1987 for ozone-depleting substances
ASEAN Haze Agreement 2002
Indoor air pollution major mortality burden (course cites ~3.2M deaths/y)

concepts.name: Air pollution definition and types
concepts.note: Presence of substances at concentration/duration causing adverse effects on humans, animals, plants, environment, or comfort. Outdoor (ambient) vs indoor (household). Outdoor varies with sources and meteorology.

concepts.name: Pollutant classification
concepts.note: Primary emitted directly; secondary formed by atmospheric reactions. Criteria pollutants are regulated common ambient pollutants; non-criteria include many toxics. Stationary, mobile, and area sources structure inventories.

concepts.name: Control technologies
concepts.note: Particulates: cyclones, ESPs, fabric filters -- often 95-99% removal industrially. Gaseous SO2: FGD (wet limestone; stoichiometry >1). Combustion stoichiometry problems link coal S/ash to SO2 and fly-ash.

concepts.name: Ozone hole and protocols
concepts.note: Stratospheric ozone depletion linked to CFCs/halons; Montreal Protocol (1987) is key international control. Regional haze (ASEAN 2002, ratified by 2015) addresses transboundary smoke.

definitions.definition: Any substance not part of natural air composition, or present at higher-than-natural concentration.
Atmospheric air in its natural state that supports life on Earth.
Common pollutants for which ambient air quality standards are set.
Formed in the atmosphere from precursors via chemical/photochemical reactions.

mustRemember: Definition = concentration OR duration causing harm/interference
Primary/secondary and stationary/mobile/area -- two orthogonal classifications
Tropospheric O3 is secondary; stratospheric O3 depletion is different
Coal S -> SO2 emission stoichiometry is a recurring numerical

weeks.title: Climate Change: Scientific Basis, Mitigation and Adaptation
examFlags: Weather = short-term; climate = long-term statistics (decades+)
GHGs: CO2, CH4, N2O, CFCs, H2O vapor -- transparent to SW, trap IR
GWP: CO2 = 1 by definition
Enhanced greenhouse effect from anthropogenic GHG buildup
Albedo feedback: ice loss -> lower albedo -> more warming
UNFCCC 1992 -> Kyoto 1997 (force 2005) -> Paris 2015 (COP21)
Kyoto Annex I ~5.2% below 1990; Doha -18% by 2020
IPCC + Al Gore Nobel Peace Prize 2007

concepts.name: Greenhouse effect vs global warming
concepts.note: Natural GHGs keep Earth habitable by absorbing outgoing IR. Extra anthropogenic GHGs enhance the effect, raising average temperatures and shifting extremes. Global warming is the temperature-rise component of broader climate change.

concepts.name: GWP and climate indicators
concepts.note: GWP measures energy absorbed by a GHG relative to CO2 over a chosen horizon. Indicators include temperature anomalies, sea ice minima, sea level, ocean heat. Course notes warming ~0.18 C/decade since 1981.

concepts.name: International climate regime
concepts.note: UNFCCC opened 1992 at Rio. Kyoto (1997, force 2005) set binding Annex I targets for CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6. Paris (2015) uses NDCs toward well-below-2 C / pursue 1.5 C. IPCC assesses science.

concepts.name: Mitigation vs adaptation
concepts.note: Mitigation reduces emissions/enhances sinks; adaptation reduces vulnerability to locked-in impacts. Both required.

definitions.definition: Statistical description of weather (averages and extremes) over decades to millennia.
Long-term shifts in temperature and weather patterns from natural and/or anthropogenic causes.
Index of energy a GHG traps relative to same mass of CO2 over a time horizon; CO2 GWP=1.
Fraction of incident solar radiation reflected; higher albedo tends to cool.

comparisons.title: Kyoto vs Paris
rows: CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6

mustRemember: Do not confuse weather with climate
Five major GHG contributors: CO2, CH4, N2O, CFCs, H2O
IPCC provides assessments; Nobel 2007 with Al Gore

weeks.title: Renewable Energy I (Solar and Wind Energy)
examFlags: Renewable = replenished at rate >= rate of use
Energy trilemma: Security, Equity, Environmental sustainability (SEE)
Incoming solar ~5.4 million EJ/year
Renewables ~12.6% of total final energy consumption (2020, course)
Betz limit CP,max = 16/27 ~ 59.3%
Pwind,max = (16/27)(1/2)rho A v^3 = (8/27) rho A v^3
Wind power proportional to rho A v^3 -- velocity cubed dominates
Intermittency -> need storage (batteries, thermal, pumped hydro)

concepts.name: Energy trilemma
concepts.note: Healthy energy systems are secure, equitable and environmentally sustainable (World Energy Council). Renewables help climate goals (Paris) and can deliver socio-economic co-benefits beyond CO2 cuts.

concepts.name: Solar technologies
concepts.note: Resource vs technical potential distinction matters. PV converts light to electricity; CSP/solar towers concentrate heat. Passive solar (direct gain, daylighting) reduces building loads. Sample CSP land-area problems use heliostat and heat-to-electric efficiencies.

concepts.name: Wind energy and Betz
concepts.note: Turbines convert kinetic energy of air; power in wind scales with rho A v^3. Betz law: no turbine can extract more than 16/27 of wind kinetic energy via rotor. Capacity factor and efficiency adjust theoretical max to annual energy. Onshore vs offshore trade resource quality vs cost/impacts.

concepts.name: Storage and intermittency
concepts.note: Solar/wind output does not always match demand; storage shifts energy in time. Thermal and electrical storage enable high renewable shares.

definitions.definition: Energy continually replenished by natural processes at a rate equal to or exceeding its rate of use.
Ratio of power extracted by a wind turbine to power available in the wind; Betz maximum is 16/27.
Resource potential constrained by technology performance, siting and system limits.
Actual energy produced over a period divided by energy if operating at rated capacity continuously.

mustRemember: SEE trilemma mnemonic: Security, Equity, Environment
P proportional to v^3 -- doubling wind speed -> 8x power
CP is <= Betz; real turbines lower due to losses + CF
Renewables defined by replenishment rate, not zero impact

weeks.title: Renewable Energy II (Geothermal, Ocean, Hydro, Bioenergy)
examFlags: Geothermal origins: primordial heat + radiogenic decay + solar-heated shallow ground
EGS: stimulate hot dry rock / low-permeability reservoirs
Geothermal heat Q = m c DeltaT (district heating example)
Tidal potential ~1200 TWh/y (smallest ocean); OTEC ~44000; wave ~29500 TWh/y
Tidal stream useful when flow ~>= 1.5-2 m/s; spring vs neap tides
Deep-water wave: PW ~ (rho g^2 H^2 T)/32 per unit crest width
Hydropower: PE = m g z; ehydro = Pelec/(m_dot g z)
Fast pyrolysis: ~400-600 C, O2-absent -> bio-oil/syngas/char

concepts.name: Geothermal and EGS
concepts.note: Thermal energy from subsurface; steam/hot water for heat or electricity. High-T systems cluster near volcanic/tectonic activity. EGS creates connectivity in hot dry rock via hydraulic stimulation. Direct use: open-loop vs closed-loop; GSHPs use shallow stable temperatures. Lifecycle GHG often <50 g CO2eq/kWh for flash steam (course).

concepts.name: Ocean energy suite
concepts.note: Five distinct ocean sources need different tech: tidal range/stream, waves, OTEC, salinity gradient, currents. Tidal barrage uses head; tidal stream uses KE. Wave mean energy density E=(1/8)rho g H^2; power = E x group velocity. OTEC uses tropical DeltaT between surface and deep water (open/closed/hybrid cycles).

concepts.name: Hydropower
concepts.note: Driven by hydrologic cycle. Types: storage (dam), run-of-river, pumped storage. Available energy mainly potential energy of head z. Multipurpose reservoirs serve irrigation, flood control, water supply besides power.

concepts.name: Bioenergy / pyrolysis
concepts.note: Biomass pathways include combustion, gasification and pyrolysis. Fast pyrolysis is low-to-moderate temperature decomposition without oxygen producing liquid bio-oil plus gases and char.

definitions.definition: Engineered geothermal reservoir created by stimulating permeability in hot rock lacking natural fluid/productivity.
Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion -- power from temperature difference between warm surface and cold deep ocean water.
Elevation difference from reservoir water surface to turbine axis used in hydropower energy calculations.
Thermal decomposition of organic material in absence (or near-absence) of oxygen; fast pyrolysis favors liquid bio-oil.

numbers.label: Geothermal example heat
numbers.value: 42 TJ/y (75 C, 20 L/s, 170 d, DeltaT=35 C)

numbers.label: Hydro example
numbers.value: 150 MW, z=35 m, Q=500 m^3/s -> compute ehydro

mustRemember: Rank ocean potentials: OTEC >> wave >> tidal (as taught)
Hydro efficiency uses head z, not kinetic of river alone
EGS = engineered permeability in hot dry rock
Wave power deep water proportional to H^2 T

weeks.title: Industrial Ecology and Circular Economy
examFlags: Urban metabolism = anabolism + catabolism of cities
Linear = Take-Make-Waste; Circular = Borrow-Use-Return
Closing the loop reduces virgin extraction and waste emissions
Industrial ecology: industry as ecosystem with symbiotic flows
Linear throughput runs down the parent ecosystem

concepts.name: Urban metabolism
concepts.note: Cities resemble organisms exchanging materials, energy and information. Anabolism builds urban stocks; catabolism generates wastes/emissions. Mapping flows reveals unsustainable linear throughput from nature through economy back as pollution.

concepts.name: Linear vs circular economy
concepts.note: Linear metabolism takes resources, makes products, discards waste -- depleting natural capital. Circular approach borrows resources intending replacement/reuse, cycling materials and energy. Benefits: less extraction, less landfill/emissions, new business models.

concepts.name: Industrial ecology and closing loops
concepts.note: Applies ecological principles to industrial systems: waste of one process becomes input to another (industrial symbiosis). Complements product design for durability, remanufacturing and recycling.

definitions.definition: Economic model that keeps products/materials in use via reuse, repair, remanufacture and recycling, minimizing virgin inputs and waste.
Sum of technical and socioeconomic processes in cities resulting in growth, energy production and waste elimination (flows of matter/energy).
Study and design of industrial systems to mimic ecosystems, optimizing material and energy cycles.
Take-make-waste production/consumption pattern with one-way throughput of materials and energy.

numbers.label: Conceptual shift emphasized
numbers.value: From linear urban subsystem to closed-loop economy

numbers.label: Core CE strategies
numbers.value: Reuse, remanufacture, recycle, design out waste

weeks.title: Water Quality, Reuse and Recycling
examFlags: Salt water ~97.5%; freshwater ~2.5%; usable freshwater tiny fraction
Withdrawals = consumption + returns; municipal WW often ~80% of water use (India cities ~87%)
DO, BOD (3 d @ 27 C India), COD, N species key parameters
DO sag / oxygen deficit from BOD loading
NSF-WQI: weighted Qi; DO weight 0.17, fecal coliform 0.16
WQI legend: 90-100 Excellent ... 0-25 Very Bad
NGT est. 18.10.2010; dispose aim within 6 months; seats: Delhi + Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai
Discharge standards differ: inland surface / sewers / irrigation / marine

concepts.name: Hydrologic cycle and water quantity
concepts.note: Global stocks dominated by salt water; usable freshwater is scarce. Off-stream vs instream uses; environmental flows protect ecosystems. Per-capita use differs sharply developed vs developing.

concepts.name: Water quality parameters
concepts.note: Physical/chemical/biological indicators: SS, pH, temperature, oil and grease, residual Cl2, NH3-N, TKN, BOD, COD. Oxygen-demanding wastes create DO sag in rivers. Nitrogen species drive eutrophication risk.

concepts.name: WQI
concepts.note: Aggregates multiple parameters into one comparable index (Horton 1965; NSF 1970 Delphi). NSF weights: DO 0.17, fecal coliform 0.16, pH 0.11, BOD 0.11, temp change 0.10, phosphate 0.10 (+ others). Enables spatial/temporal comparison.

concepts.name: NGT and reuse
concepts.note: NGT Act 2010 creates specialized green tribunal guided by natural justice. Sets/enforces discharge norms (incl. revised STP standards 2018). Zero liquid discharge aspiration and tertiary treatment enable reuse/recycling.

definitions.definition: Water extracted from surface or groundwater sources.
Withdrawn water not returned (e.g., evaporated, incorporated into products, transpired).
Biochemical oxygen demand -- oxygen used by microbes to stabilize organic matter; Indian standard often BOD3 at 27 C.
Single aggregated score representing overall water quality from multiple weighted parameters.

numbers.label: Municipal WW as % of water use

mustRemember: BOD3 @ 27 C is Indian convention (not always BOD5 @ 20 C)
NGT principal bench New Delhi; 4 other places

weeks.title: Solid Waste Management (including E-waste)
examFlags: Waste hierarchy: Prevent > Reuse > Recycle > Recover > Dispose
4Rs: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Recover (source reduction first)
Solid waste includes containerized liquid/gas wastes in definition
Open dumps -> air (VOCs, CH4 explosions), water, soil contamination
Moisture, TS, VS, FS characterization maths
MSW composition varies; organics often large in Indian cities
E-waste Rules 2011 (India); EPR concepts

concepts.name: ISWM and hierarchy
concepts.note: Integrated Solid Waste Management coordinates generation through disposal with hierarchy prioritizing prevention and material recovery over landfilling. Green design and labeling support source reduction.

concepts.name: MSW generation and composition
concepts.note: Generation rates rise with income/urbanization. Composition (organics, paper, plastics, metals, inert) drives collection, treatment and landfill design. Wet-weight moisture and volatile solids determine biological treatment suitability.

concepts.name: Treatment and disposal
concepts.note: Options: recycling, biological treatment, thermal, sanitary landfill. Open dumping is unacceptable due to multi-media pollution. Engineered landfills control leachate and landfill gas.

concepts.name: E-waste
concepts.note: Fast-growing stream with toxic and valuable fractions. Requires segregated collection, authorized recyclers and Extended Producer Responsibility under e-waste rules.

definitions.definition: Waste neither liquid nor gaseous in free form; containerized liquid/gaseous wastes are also included under solid waste in regulatory framing.
Priority order preferring prevention and reuse over recycling, recovery and last-resort disposal.
Fraction of total solids lost on ignition; proxy for organic content available for biodegradation.
System approach selecting complementary technologies and policies across the waste chain.

comparisons.title: Open dump vs Sanitary landfill
rows: Disposal of last resort in hierarchy

numbers.value: 40% moisture -> TS=60%; if 50/60 lost on ignition -> VS=83.3% of TS

numbers.label: Open dump hazards
numbers.value: Air, SW/GW, soil, methane explosion risk

weeks.title: Noise Pollution
examFlags: lambda = c/f ; period p=1/f
Lp = 20 log(Prms/P0); P0=20 uPa = 0 dB
c ~ 20.05*sqrt(T) (T in K)
I = W/(4 pi r^2) inverse square; Delta Lp ~ -20 log(r2/r1) -> -6 dB per distance doubling
Line source: intensity proportional to 1/r (not 1/r^2)
Equal sources: two equal levels -> +3 dB
85 dB(A) 8-h occupational risk threshold (course)
Leq, Ldn, LN rating systems; A-weighting mimics ear

concepts.name: Sound fundamentals
concepts.note: Sound needs a medium; alternating compression/rarefaction. Human hearing ~20 uPa to 200 Pa (many orders -> log dB scale). Sound power Lw, intensity LI, pressure Lp related but instruments measure pressure.

concepts.name: Decibel arithmetic
concepts.note: Logarithmic: +10 dB ~ 10x intensity. Adding incoherent sources uses energy sum; two equal 50 dB -> 53 dB. Large level differences -> sum ~ louder source.

concepts.name: Propagation and ratings
concepts.note: Point-source outdoor spreading follows inverse square (-6 dB per doubling distance). Line sources (roads) fall ~3 dB per doubling. Leq energy-averages fluctuating noise; Ldn penalizes night. A-weighting used for environmental/occupational limits.

concepts.name: Effects and control
concepts.note: TTS/PTS hearing loss, annoyance, sleep disturbance, cardiovascular stress. Control: source, path (barriers), receiver (PPE). CPCB zone standards and workplace limits apply.

definitions.definition: Unwanted sound producing undesired physiological or psychological effects, or interfering with activities.
Lp=20 log(Prms/20 uPa) in dB; 0 dB is nominal threshold of hearing.
Equivalent continuous sound level with the same total energy as a time-varying noise over the measurement period.
For a point source in free field, intensity falls as 1/r^2, so SPL drops ~6 dB when distance doubles.

mustRemember: -6 dB rule for point sources when distance doubles
Noise is energy pollution -- hearing damage can be permanent

weeks.title: Ecology and Soil Pollution
examFlags: Ecology from oikos = house; study of organisms at home
Energy flow unidirectional; mass/nutrients cyclic
Trophic levels: producers -> herbivores -> carnivores
Logistic growth: exponential modified by carrying capacity K
BCF = Cbiota/Cwater (L/kg); correlates with Kow
Bioaccumulation vs biomagnification vs bioconcentration
USLE: A = R K L S C P
USLE unit plot: 72.6 ft x 5.5 ft, 9% slope

concepts.name: Ecosystem structure and function
concepts.note: Ecosystem = community + abiotic environment with mass/energy flows and functional stability. Biosphere aggregates all ecosystems. Photosynthesis is a redox process fixing C and releasing O2; productivity measures biomass/energy capture.

concepts.name: Niche, food webs, pyramids
concepts.note: Ecological niche is the role/position of a species. Food chains link into webs; trophic pyramids of numbers/biomass/energy. Biomagnification elevates concentrations up the chain (classic DDT lake example).

concepts.name: BCF and toxic organics
concepts.note: Bioconcentration compares tissue to water; BCF often rises with hydrophobicity (log BCF ~ log Kow). Bioaccumulation includes diet; biomagnification is trophic-level increase. Cadmium/DDT tables show enormous concentration factors.

concepts.name: Soil pollution and USLE
concepts.note: Soil degradation via erosion, salinization, contaminants, overgrazing. Universal Soil Loss Equation estimates average annual soil loss A using rainfall erosivity R, soil erodibility K, slope length/steepness LS, cover C and practice P.

definitions.definition: Study of interrelationships between organisms (and groups) and their biotic/abiotic environment.
Functional role and position of a species in its ecosystem, including resource use and interactions.
Cbiota/Cwater; units L water/kg tissue.
Universal Soil Loss Equation A=RKLSCP estimating sheet/rill erosion soil loss.

mustRemember: USLE letters: R K L S C P

weeks.title: Environmental Policies and Legislation
examFlags: Movements: Bishnoi (Khejri), Chipko (1973), Appiko (1982-83), Jungle Bachao
Water Act 1974; Air Act 1981 (am. 1987); EPA 1986 (am. 1991)
Act = law/substance; Rules = procedure under the Act
HW Rules 1989; BMW 1998; MSW 2000/2016; Batteries 2001; Plastic/E-waste 2011; C&D 2016
NGT Act 2010; principles of natural justice; 6-month disposal endeavor
Industrial Revolutions 1-5 linked to new pollution/e-waste/REE streams
Landmark PILs / M.C. Mehta cases; rapid EIA case study lecture

concepts.name: Environmental movement (India)
concepts.note: Community forest protection predates modern law: Bishnoi sacrifice for Khejri trees; Chipko tree-hugging in Himalaya (Bahuguna marches; Right Livelihood Award 1987); Appiko in Western Ghats; Jungle Bachao. Movements shaped public opinion preceding statutes.

concepts.name: Core Indian environmental statutes
concepts.note: Water Act 1974 created CPCB/SPCBs for prevention/control of water pollution. Air Act 1981 parallels for air with consent regime. Umbrella EPA 1986 empowers Central Government post-Bhopal era for protection/improvement and wide rule-making.

concepts.name: Rules ecosystem
concepts.note: Sectoral Rules under EPA/related Acts govern hazardous waste, biomedical, fly ash, MSW, batteries, plastics, e-waste, C&D waste -- updated as streams emerge. Acts are slower to pass; Rules are more agile procedures.

concepts.name: NGT and judgments / EIA
concepts.note: NGT provides specialized, expeditious environmental adjudication. Course covers important legal judgments and NGT orders plus a rapid EIA case -- EIA as predictive, participatory decision tool linked to clearance conditions.

definitions.definition: An Act is the statute prescribing substantive law (what must be done); Rules are subordinate legislation detailing procedures to implement the Act.
Umbrella Indian law empowering the Centre to protect and improve environment, set standards, and regulate hazardous substances.
National Green Tribunal -- specialized body (2010) for effective disposal of environmental cases, guided by natural justice.
Environmental Impact Assessment -- systematic prediction and evaluation of environmental effects of a proposed project before decision.

comparisons.title: Water Act vs Air Act vs EPA

mustRemember: NGT not bound by CPC 1908; natural justice; try dispose in 6 months
